originality.rationale: Inoue and Aki (published online 2006-06-17) give a conditional multivariate run-count generating function, so the finite distributions and moment extraction are prior territory. The assessed claim is the asymptotic all-length sign phase, Pell-indexed tangency family, and exceptional second-order critical-window law. Examination of the full primary conditional-run paper, its applications, the Bernoulli predecessor, and the nearby Markov-run CLT paper found no explicit or stronger stated asymptotic phase classification. Priority risk remains because a broad generating function encodes all finite moments implicitly.
residual_risks: Inoue–Aki conditional generating functions imply finite conditional run moments in principle. A specialist may classify the new phase theorem as an implicit corollary even if the sign/Pell geometry is not stated.
Not all run-statistics monographs, conference proceedings, or derivative literature were accessible or inspected; priority remains same-model only.
Exact-length patterns with endpoint conventions could have an alternative equivalent phase statement.

value.rationale: The run-length spectrum is a natural fixed-composition randomness-test statistic. Its cross-covariance has a complete positive/negative density classification: a positive phase requires a length ratio exceeding an explicit sharp threshold, exemplified by the minimal pair (1,9) and p between 3/5 and 3/4. Arithmetic Pell tangencies and the exceptional inverse-N cancellation at (1,8) explain boundary behavior not visible from generic moment recurrences. The phase is not an arbitrary finite example, nor a claimed new general run-distribution method.
